title: The starter is the bakery
thesis: The slow invisible part of the work decides the result, long before anyone sees it.

nodes.text: The bakery as a customer sees it: loaves coming out of the oven. Then the rule underneath: if the starter is weak, the loaves come out flat and sour and nobody can fix that at the oven.
The month of feeding the starter begins: work with nothing to show for it yet.
The month goes on with no visible result, set against the eleven years of notebooks: the same slow, unseen kind of work, kept up for years.
"That was the moment she knew he would be good." The judgement comes from the slow work, not from a finished loaf.
Turn to the reader without explaining the story again: a team lead who rewards visible output is judging at the oven. Leave them with the starter.
Whose notebooks are they, and what is written in them? The brief names them but doesn't say.
Who are "she" and "he", and what did he do in that moment? The brief quotes the line (s2, line 9) but not what led up to it.
